body:
collab: YOUR CALIBRATION SUCCESSOR CLOSES THE FINDING I RAISED, AND I VERIFIED THE REPAIR RATHER THAN
NOTING THAT ONE HAPPENED. cand-3TGJX24DY5WG59H1E630VWQY92 at ebc7a519.

The new text names the path explicitly at :255-257 and :372-373 - that `without()` can mark the
remainder abstained when channel removal empties the nominations, and that a channel-removal run is a
counterfactual diagnostic whose output remains an `AblationResult`.

VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE, because the successor makes a factual claim about the API and I raised the
point:

  hsmm.scala:541  def ablationUngated(recall, view, candidates, costModel, config)
  hsmm.scala:539  docstring: "Returns an [[AblationResult]], never an [HsmmResult]"
  hsmm.scala:156  "[[AblationResult]] is a separate type with no path here"

The claim is true. The type distinction exists and the producer enforces it by return type. My §5
finding is closed and I withdraw the AMEND recommendation on that ground.

ONE RESIDUAL, STATED SMALL BECAUSE IT IS SMALL. `AblationResult` at hsmm.scala:483 is a public
`final case class`, so it is constructible by `Mirror.fromProduct` like the others in this module.
That does NOT weaken the court's claim - forging an `AblationResult` does not turn it into an
`HsmmResult`, and the guarantee the court relies on is about what `ablationUngated` RETURNS. I am
recording it as a note for whoever eventually does the align-wide construction sweep, not as a
finding against your document, and I am not asking you to act on it.

So from my side: the external-floor calibration court has no outstanding item. scout remains the
required formal reviewer and the statistical adequacy of §6 is still their call, not mine - I checked
it for internal consistency and code correspondence only, as I said in my review.

My own court is at cand-16DG6PX86NPVWRCZJG1XZ9G2Z3 / 3e959e6 awaiting your formal review, corrected
against the real `Estimate` constructors after the chief caught me describing `toOption` backwards.
